title: Musk says TSMC won't run Terafab AI chip complex
gist: Elon Musk said Tesla and SpaceX will build and operate Terafab, their planned AI chip manufacturing complex in Texas, ruling out TSMC running it and allowing only a possible sublease. Intel's CEO said Intel remains a partner, and the actual division of roles is still unspecified.

insights.claim: Elon Musk says Tesla and SpaceX will build and operate the planned Terafab AI chip complex in Texas themselves, ruling out TSMC taking control of it.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Vertical integration into chip manufacturing by Tesla and SpaceX remains the stated plan.
insights.locator: Elon Musk Rules Out Potential TSMC Role in Terafab Operations

insights.claim: Musk said any TSMC participation in Terafab could be limited to subleasing part of the complex, and last week's reported talks produced no confirmed agreement or defined TSMC responsibilities.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: TSMC upside from Terafab is optional and unquantified; do not model it as a contract.
insights.locator: Musk made the clarification on Wednesday

insights.claim: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan told Bloomberg News that Intel would remain part of the Terafab venture, and the article notes a possible TSMC sublease would not by itself mean Intel is replaced.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Intel's Terafab role appears intact for now; monitor for how responsibilities are split.

insights.claim: The announcement clarifies Musk's intended management structure more than the practical arrangements, and it is still unexplained how responsibilities would be divided among Tesla, SpaceX, Intel and TSMC or whether binding commitments will result.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Treat Terafab partner announcements as unconfirmed until binding terms are disclosed.
